Automated Model Briefing

⚠ AI-generated text — may be wrong, incomplete, or overconfident. This is automated commentary on experimental model output, not flight advice and not a weather forecast. It has not been reviewed by a meteorologist.

Overall Assessment — Saturday is a quiet day between storms, with light winds and weak to moderate thermals. Thermal strength (w*) peaks around 200–370 ft/min between late morning and mid-afternoon, and the best climbs are at the lower valley-edge sites (McClellan, Hallelujah, Duck Hill, Rainbow Ridge), although winds don't line up with every launch. Wind across the Sierra crest stays light at 8–16 knots from the west to southwest, the ECMWF model agrees with this model on that flow, and NWS Reno also expects light winds and clear flying weather Saturday. The model has trended toward weaker thermals and more cloud than the previous run, and thermals fade from about 3pm as high cloud moves in by 4pm.

Site Breakdown

Hallelujah Favorable — A west wind sets in by early afternoon with good thermals and steadily building ridge lift that carries into the evening.
Window: 12:30pm–4:15pm
Peak thermal strength is 319 ft/min at 1pm, with a thermal top near 3,100 ft AGL from 1–3pm. Wind is 5–9 mph from the west, and ridge lift builds from +152 ft/min at 1pm to +323 ft/min at 4pm, giving good evening ridge soaring as thermals fade. At 3pm about two thirds of the sky has cloud with its base about 3,100 ft above launch, right at the thermal top and above the 7,915 ft above sea level (MSL) freezing level, so stay clear of cloud base. Wind direction turns up to 34 degrees within one 100 m layer, but the combined shear stays low at 5 mph per 100 m because winds are light. Mean cloud cover has risen from 5% to 52% since the previous run.
McClellan Favorable — Light south to southeast wind on launch for most of the day, with the best thermals in the area.
Window: 10am–3:30pm
Peak thermal strength is 328 ft/min at 1pm, with a thermal top near 2,600–2,750 ft AGL from 1–3pm. Surface wind stays 3–5 mph from the south to southeast. Wind 3,000 ft above ground is 12–14 mph from the southwest, so expect drift on climb-outs. Cloud base (the height where rising thermals form cloud, LCL) is well above the thermal top, so thermals are not capped by cloud. At 4pm the wind turns west, crossing launch.

Not recommended today (7) — click a row for details

Kingsbury grade Marginal — A light southeast breeze lines up with launch only around midday, and thermals are weak in stable air.
Window: 11am–1pm
Peak thermal strength is about 213 ft/min with a thermal top (height of the mixed layer, PBLH) near 1,457–1,634 ft above ground (AGL). Wind is 2–4 mph from the east-southeast in the window. Stable air blocks most of the slope, so expect little ridge lift. From 2pm the wind turns west at 7–12 mph, putting launch on the downwind side with sinking air. Peak thermal strength is down from 277 to 213 ft/min since the previous run.
Slide Mountain Marginal — Only a short late-morning sled window with a light southeast wind, very weak thermals, and sinking air on launch in the afternoon.
Window: 10am–11:30am
Peak thermal strength is only about 131 ft/min with a thermal top under 800 ft AGL. Wind is 4 mph from the southeast to south-southeast in the window. Stable air blocks most of the slope below launch, so the ridge-lift numbers are overstated. From 2pm a southwest wind of 8–14 mph puts launch on the sinking side, down to -334 ft/min at 3pm. Wind direction turns up to 37 degrees within one 100 m layer. The summit station read well below the model's wind Friday night but gusted to 52 mph. Since the previous run, peak thermals fell from 220 to 159 ft/min and time with launch-aligned light wind dropped from 67% to 19%.
West McClellan Marginal — The wind is behind or across launch through midday, so it lines up only in the morning and mid-afternoon.
Window: 3pm–4:15pm
From 3pm the wind lines up from the west-southwest at 8–13 mph, with ridge lift of +175 ft/min rising to +351 ft/min at 4pm. Thermals are about 192 ft/min at 3pm and gone by 4pm, with a thermal top near 2,340 ft AGL. Wind 1,000 ft above ground reaches 17 mph at 4pm. Around 9am there is also usable ridge lift (+211 ft/min at 13 mph from the west-southwest), but thermals are still weak then at about 97 ft/min. From 11am to 2pm the wind turns south to south-southeast and launch sits in slightly sinking air.
Peavine Mountain Marginal — Southwest winds put launch in sinking air all day, and they are only moderate around midday.
Window: 11am–1pm
Peak thermal strength is about 222–225 ft/min at noon to 1pm, with a thermal top of 1,273–1,710 ft AGL. Wind is 7–10 mph from the south-southwest in the window but 15–18 mph in the morning and after 2pm, and the model shows sinking air on the launch slope every hour. Cloud base is close to the thermal top and above the 7,975 ft MSL freezing level. Nearby Reno-Stead airport has been windier than the model, so winds here may be under-forecast. Peak thermal strength is down from 290 to 227 ft/min since the previous run.
Duck Hill Marginal — Strong thermals, but a south-southeast wind blows behind launch until a brief west wind around 3pm.
Window: 2:30pm–3:30pm
At 3pm thermals are about 295 ft/min with a thermal top near 4,050 ft AGL, and wind is a light 4 mph from the west, which lines up with launch. From 10am to 1pm the wind is 3–6 mph from the south-southeast, behind launch. At 4pm wind is 10 mph from the west-southwest, just outside the launch direction, with ridge lift of +94 ft/min, so evening soaring is marginal. Wind direction turns up to 55 degrees within one 100 m layer, so expect switchy air near the hill.
Daydreams Marginal — The southwest wind lines up well all day, but cloud base sits inside the thermal band and the freezing level is just above launch.
Window: 11am–4:15pm
Thermal strength holds at 251–259 ft/min from 9am to 2pm, with a thermal top near 1,900–2,500 ft AGL. Wind is 3–9 mph from the southwest, with ridge lift of +115 to +178 ft/min from 1pm to 4pm, giving good evening ridge soaring. Low cloud covers launch at 8–9am with its base only 900–1,200 ft above launch. Through the afternoon cloud base runs below the thermal top, at 993 ft above launch by 3pm, which risks being drawn into cloud. That cloud base is above the 7,796 ft MSL freezing level. Mean cloud cover has risen from 5% to 49% since the previous run.
Rainbow Ridge Unfavorable — The wind blows from behind this east-facing launch all day, with strong wind shear about 600 ft above ground.
Thermals are strong at 330–365 ft/min, with a thermal top near 3,900–4,000 ft AGL in the early afternoon. Surface wind is 3–10 mph from the southwest to west, which is a tailwind for this launch, so ridge lift is near zero. Wind shear peaks at 14 mph per 100 m with an 86-degree direction change at 571 ft AGL, which is a hazardous level.

Hazards

  • Uncertain ridge-top winds: Friday night the Slide Mountain summit station measured 26 mph gusting to 52 mph from the southwest, while the model had 41 mph. The model's mean wind was too strong but the real gusts were strong, so treat the model's high-launch and flying-height winds with lower confidence. Reno-Stead airport has also been windier than the model.
  • Cloud base inside thermals and icing: At Daydreams, Peavine Mountain and Hallelujah, cloud base sits at or below the thermal top during parts of the day and above a freezing level of roughly 7,800–7,975 ft MSL. Stay well below cloud base to avoid being drawn into cloud and icing. Low cloud also covers Daydreams at 8–9am.
  • Wind shear on low eastern sites: Rainbow Ridge shows hazardous wind shear of 14 mph per 100 m with an 86-degree direction change about 570 ft above ground. Duck Hill shows a 55-degree direction change within one 100 m layer, so expect bumpy, switchy air close to the terrain.
  • Morning snow and road access: NWS Reno has a Winter Storm Warning until 10am Saturday for the Lake Tahoe zones and mentions lingering snow and slick roads. This may affect access to the higher Carson Range launches early in the day.
  • Afternoon southwest wind on high launches: From about 2pm the southwest to west wind strengthens at Peavine Mountain (13–18 mph) and Slide Mountain (8–14 mph). Both launches sit in sinking air, down to -334 ft/min at Slide at 3pm.
